page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.2xlarge is an Arm-based compute-optimized instance powered by an Ampere Altra processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The server provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an arm64 instruction set with AES cryptographic extensions running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance includes no integrated local storage or GPU hardware, relying on external block storage, and operates with a baseline network speed of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results show steady performance across multi-threaded evaluations with lower relative single-thread metrics. In multi-threaded compute tests, stress-ng recorded 14295.27 and Geekbench multi-core achieved 6139.0, both performing in the middle tier. Software compilation using Clang reached 9709.0, while static web serving throughput measured 10.79 GB/sec and Redis SET performance delivered 11.05 million operations per second. In contrast, single-threaded processing reflects architectural limitations, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 1104.0 and gzip compression throughput of 23.76 GB/sec.

The server architecture provides predictable execution due to dedicated physical core mapping without simultaneous multithreading contention. Because single-thread speeds and memory capacities are modest, the instance is less suited for heavy in-memory databases, large language models, or single-threaded legacy applications. It offers efficient execution for horizontally scalable environments, static web serving, containerized microservices, and distributed build pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the 64-bit Arm architecture, featuring an 8-core Ampere Altra processor clocked at 2.8 GHz and 16.0 GB of system memory. Operating without local storage or GPU accelerators, the instance utilizes remote block volumes and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. Multi-threaded benchmark testing shows balanced mid-tier results, reaching 14295.27 in stress-ng multi-core and 11.05 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core metrics like the Geekbench single-core score of 1104.0 place in the lower quartile. The dedicated 1:2 core-to-memory configuration delivers consistent per-core performance free from hyperthreading contention. This profile is effective for distributed microservices, static web delivery, continuous integration environments, and parallelized compilation tasks where multi-core scaling is prioritized over maximum single-thread clock performance.
